title: A user's security settings in Authentication Service: initial password option, skipping second-factor authentication and MFA authenticators

prose.text: The Security Settings tab of a user is where an admin sets the initial password option, lets the user skip second-factor authentication for a while and removes configured MFA authenticators; the user's record and status are in [[zidentity.users]].

prose.label: Skipping second-factor authentication.
prose.text: {{skip-second-factor}} {{skip-duration}} {{skip-hosted-admins-only}} Whether the API's skip action follows the same limits is open {{gap:skip-api-scope}}.

prose.label: Open.
prose.text: The password policy rules and the MFA factors are not given {{gap:password-policy-and-factors}}.

password-options.statement: A user must be added before security settings are configured; Change Password Settings must be enabled to modify the password configuration. Set By User makes the user set their own password and sends a password reset email, and the user can choose and configure the required authentication method; Set by Administrator has the admin set the password; Auto-generated generates one for the user, and the Copy and View icons copy or view the password.

quotes: A user must be added before configuring the security settings.
Change Password Settings: Enable to modify the password configurations.

Set By User: Select this option if the user must set their own password to access the Zscaler Admin Console. The user receives a password reset email. The user can choose and configure the required authentication method.
Set by Administrator: Select this option to set a password for the user:
Auto-generated: Select this option to auto-generate a password for the user:
Password: Use the Copy and View icons to copy or view the password.

prompt-change-default.statement: With Set by Administrator and with Auto-generated, Prompt for Password Change After the Initial Login is selected by default; for Set by Administrator the user then changes the password following the guidelines in the password policy.

evidence.after: Confirm Password: Reenter the user's password.
quotes: Prompt for Password Change After the Initial Login: This option is selected by default. The user needs to change the password by following the guidelines defined in the password policy.

evidence.after: Password: Use the Copy and View icons to copy or view the password.
quotes: Prompt for Password Change After the Initial Login: This option is selected by default.

skip-second-factor.statement: An admin can enable Skip Second-Factor Authentication for a user and, with Skip Until, select the date and time up to when the user can skip second-factor authentication, after which the user must configure it; the Add User page offers Skip Until, and on the Edit User page's Security Settings section the option is enabled under Multi-Factor Bypass as Skip Second Factor Authentication.

quotes: Skip Second-Factor Authentication: Enable if you want the user to skip second-factor authentication. For the Skip Until option, select the date and time up to when the user can skip second-factor authentication. Post this duration, the user must configure second-factor authentication.
Skip Until: Select the date and time up to when the user can skip second-factor authentication. Post this duration, the user must configure second-factor authentication.
On the Edit User page, click the Security Settings section.
Under Multi-Factor Bypass, enable Skip Second Factor Authentication.

skip-duration.statement: The Skip Until field displays the current date and time; by default MFA can be skipped for 8 hours, and the maximum limit is 5 days.

quotes: The Skip Until field appears, displaying the current date and time.
By default, the MFA can be skipped for 8 hours.
The maximum limit is 5 days.

skip-hosted-admins-only.statement: Skipping two-factor authentication lets Authentication Service administrators log in to the subscribed Zscaler service with only a password for a short duration (the help's example: a user without the device that receives their one-time passcode); the Skip Second Factor Authentication option is only available for hosted admins and not for admins authenticating via the external IdP.

quotes: Authentication Service administrators can skip two-factor authentication (2FA) for a short duration and use only their password to log in to the subscribed Zscaler service.
For example, if a user does not have the device on which they receive the one-time passcode (OTP) for authentication, they can be allowed to skip 2FA temporarily.
The Skip Second Factor Authentication option is only available for hosted admins and not for admins authenticating via the external Identity provider (IdP).

authenticators.statement: Security settings show each MFA method configured for a user with the date and time it was last used to log in to the Zscaler Admin Console; an admin can delete authenticators except the email authenticator, and the user is then prompted to reconfigure MFA the next time they log in to the Zscaler Admin Console.

quotes: MFA Authenticator: Displays the MFA method configured for a user and the date and time it was last used to log in to Zscaler Admin Console.
Click the Delete icon to remove the configured MFA option. The user is then prompted to reconfigure MFA the next time they log in to the Zscaler Admin Console.
You can also view the multi-factor authenticators that are configured for the user.
You can choose to delete the authenticators, except the email authenticator.

skip-api-scope.title: Whether the API's skip-MFA action follows the console's duration, maximum and hosted-admin limits
skip-api-scope.detail: The console page limits skipping to hosted admins with an 8-hour default and a 5-day maximum. The published zid API's POST /users/{id}:setskipmfa takes only a timestamp, described as when the MFA skip action was set; whether it applies the same duration, maximum or hosted-admin restriction is not stated. The Add User and Edit User pages offer the option without naming the hosted-admin restriction, and what it does for an IdP-authenticated user is not stated.

password-policy-and-factors.title: The password policy rules and the MFA factors
password-policy-and-factors.detail: The pages point to the password policy without giving its rules, and name an email authenticator, one-time passcodes and one-time token or link methods without listing the available MFA factors.
